title: DD token overhead: JSON bloat is in MCP get, not in retrieve count
body:
Measure before assuming retrieval volume is the cost. Production telemetry showed 98% abstention and 1.17 memories per injection (max 3); the 600-token budget fits about 2 hits. The PreToolUse hook injects plain text with ~7% overhead, MCP retrieve JSON adds ~178 B per hit plus a 119 B envelope (~26%), but MCP get returns the whole atom (~7 KB, ~90% metadata such as evidence_state). Target get's payload and the retrieval forms first.

Why: Measured on 2026-09-22 against ~/.dd-data/supermem-*/index.sqlite (1118 retrieval events) and the 34 active atoms. deriveForms makes micro = full behavior_delta (avg 667 B), and short == full in 29/34 atoms, so the form ladder barely compacts. Byte counts use the plugin's bytes/3 estimate, not a real tokenizer.

evidence.summary: get handler returns the full atom plus freshness, relations and outcomes; jsonResult serializes it verbatim
deriveForms: micro = behavior_delta, short = micro + Why, full = short + alternatives
avg micro 667 B, hit JSON 846 B, envelope 119 B, full atom 7036 B, short==full 29/34

v1.trigger: When investigating DD token cost, JSON overhead, or the claim that too many small memories are retrieved
